extracted.intended_audience: PR agencies, in-house communications and entrant teams submitting work to the PR Lions (Cannes Lions) awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and judging rubric for preparing and submitting PR campaign entries to the PR Lions (Cannes Lions) awards, including category definitions, judging weights, required materials and the written submission questions and prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of criteria will be considered during judging, weighted as follows: 20% idea; 30% PR strategy; 20% PR execution; 30% impact and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges allocate scores according to these weightings when assessing entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury expectations – strategic earned media & storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy rooted in earned media that has real impact, beyond likes and impressions. Work that has storytelling at its core and establishes, protects or enhances the reputation and business of an organisation or brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Jury looks for a strong insight, impressive execution and real results that link back to the objective; considered strategy thoughtfully designed at every touchpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of impact & approver requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You'll be required provide proof of impact, supported by verifiable evidence; this information will not be shared with the Jury, but will be used to verify claims made in your entry materials. You'll also be required to provide details of a senior executive from both the brand and the entrant company (CEO, CMO or equivalent) who can formally approve the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide verifiable evidence to support claims; misrepresentation may result in withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period
rubrics_metrics.description: Work will need to have been executed during the eligibility period of 06 February 2025 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only submissions executed within these dates are eligible for judging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry frequency limits and Section E restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The same piece of work can be entered up to four times in PR. Exceptions: The same piece of work may only be entered once in ‘A. PR: Sectors’. The work in Section E: Excellence in PR Craft can only be submitted and paid for by independent PR agencies or companies owned by a PR network or independent PR network. The same piece of work can be entered only once in each category within this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check section-specific rules before submitting duplicates; Section E requires independent agency status and limits per-category entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry completion and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You can fill in the form in any order and save your progress at any time while it’s still in the pending stage. However, please only check out when your entry is 100% complete as no changes can be made to your entry once you’ve clicked 'Submit' and 'Checkout'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure entry is final before checkout; use save-as-you-go but finalize only when complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry presentation tips
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the most impressive part of your campaign and find a category that showcases it. Provide tangible results that demonstrate impact. Remember the Jury are from all over the world, so provide context throughout your entry to ensure they understand the significance of your results and the relevance of your insight. The Jury look at hundreds of pieces of work, use storytelling in the written submission and case film to help your work stand out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the category that highlights the campaign's strongest aspect; provide context and evidence; use storytelling to stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A01 Consumer Goods
rubrics_metrics.description: All fast-moving and durable consumer goods, including but not limited to, food and beverages, toiletries, cleaning products, other household goods, other FMCGs, clothing and accessories, furniture, and consumer electronics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fast-food entries should be entered into A04. Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A02 Healthcare
rubrics_metrics.description: Pharma, OTC drugs, wellness. If the work has been created for a Charity/NFP then this should be entered into A07.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter relevant charity/NFP work in A07 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A03 Automotive
rubrics_metrics.description: Vehicles, other automobiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A04 Travel, Leisure, Retail, Restaurants & Fast-Food Chains
rubrics_metrics.description: All transport- and travel-related services, including public transport and tourism boards. All entertainment- and leisure-related services, including museums, festivals and gyms. All shops, including online shopping, opticians, hairdressers and estate agents. All restaurants and fast food chains, including cafés and bars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All fast-food entries should be entered here rather than A01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A05 Media/Entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Music, film, television, publications and media, books, news, digital platforms and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A06 Consumer Services/Business to Business
rubrics_metrics.description: All commercial public services, legal, financial, B2B technology, consultancies and professional services, other business services, internal and corporate communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category A07 Not-for-Profit / Charity / Government
rubrics_metrics.description: Government, public information, NGOs, military, charities, non-profit organisations. All corporate social responsibility work should be entered in the relevant sector and/or F07. Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility category in section F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B01 Social Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrating public relations and social media storytelling that build brand awareness and advocacy. The work should demonstrate how social media was harnessed to increase brand awareness and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on how social/digital platforms were leveraged to support or execute the PR campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B02 Community Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising the development, maintenance and nurturing of brand relationships. The work should demonstrate how engaging with a brand's online community/targeted audience built its reputation and established trust and authority within the online community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B03 Real-Time Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time social activity designed to respond to and engage in the conversation around world events, public affairs and other real-world, real-time activity in a creative and meaningful way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B04 Content Creation & Production
rubrics_metrics.description: Content created and produced to entertain, inspire or educate. The work should demonstrate how the content created was audience-relevant and engaging as well as in line with brand messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B05 Content Discovery & Amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising a creative approach to content amplification and distribution in order to reach the largest potential audience. The work should demonstrate how a combination of earned, paid, shared and owned media contributed to increased brand engagement and awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category B06 Innovative Use of Influencers/Creators
rubrics_metrics.description: The creative and innovative use of influencers/creators to drive brand message and awareness to a specific audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category C01 Research, Data & Analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and data-led or actionable insights that provide a meaningful contribution or input to a public relations programme. The work should provide evidence of research or insight, quality of thinking and the development of a strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on deliberate and thoughtful introduction of insights and measurements to develop campaigns with real impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category C02 PR Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognises creative work that has a proven impact on business and reputation. The work should provide results data, as well as details of measurement tools and analysis methods used to evaluate results. Consideration will be given to tangible business results and the quality and quantity of media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on effectiveness using data, tools and tangible business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D01 Media Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: PR that puts journalism at the forefront of the campaign, with evidence of a high degree of innovation intended to engage, educate or influence editorial. The work should explain the relevance of media outcomes, including depth, quality and messaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider relevance of media outcomes and how this strategy supported desired campaign outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D02 Use of Events & Stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that uses stunts, events, event sponsorship, competitions, promotional games, street art, guerrilla marketing, launch parties, live shows, live streamed events, festivals, concerts, sporting events, etc. within traditional, digital and new emerging environments to build the value and reputation of a brand or communication project as part of a wider public relations strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judged on creative implementation of events/stunts to increase reach and achieve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D03 Launch/Relaunch
rubrics_metrics.description: Work created to launch or relaunch a product or service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D04 Brand Voice & Strategic Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Customised strategies designed to communicate a particular point of view/story of a brand/organisation in a consistently relevant way and to build an emotional connection with employees, shareholders and customers alike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D05 Use of Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing or new technology that pushes the boundaries of digital innovation to execute or support a PR campaign. This could include but is not limited to artificial intelligence, virtual reality, virtual worlds, robotics, gadgets and electronics, wearable and interactive technology, etc. Does not include prototypes of early-stage technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category D06 Employee Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications programmes or initiatives designed to inform, educate or inspire employees - engaging internal communities and cultivating strong team dynamics. The work should demonstrate innovative approaches to engaging staff, driving organisational goals and building employee loyalty and satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section E eligibility & purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Work in these categories will be judged on the demonstration of exceptional and creative best practice within the chosen PR specialism. Entries in this section can only be submitted and paid for by Independent PR agencies or companies owned by a PR network or independent PR network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same piece can only be entered once in each category within this section; intended to spotlight independent PR craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category E01 Corporate Image, Communication & Reputation Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that builds the image/raises the profile and shapes the perceptions of a corporate brand, organisation or corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category E02 Public Affairs & Lobbying
rubrics_metrics.description: Work planned to influence or inform the public policy agenda using either lobbying or wider public affairs strategies, as well as political or ballot initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category E03 Crisis Communications & Issue Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The planning and/or handling of the consequences of a crisis or an issue that may affect a company’s credibility and reputation. The work should demonstrate evidence of the planning and/or implementation of a crisis communication strategy and how the desired outcome was achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The content of entries in this category can be kept entirely confidential and used for judging purposes only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category E04 Internal Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging internal communications and activities. This includes but is not limited to change management, intended to connect employees with a company identity or message. The work should demonstrate how activities translated into measurable results, employee satisfaction and business growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category E05 Sponsorship & Brand Partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that utilised sponsorship and/or partnership programmes in order to meet specific awareness/business goals as well as to enhance the image of a brand, organisation or corporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F01 Local Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Work for brands distributed solely within a specific locality. The work should resonate with a clearly defined, local target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires comment on how the brand resonated with a specific target audience in a single locality or market (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F02 Challenger Brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their approach in response to competitor pressure by challenging the status quo to create game-changing work that uses progressive thinking and innovative creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the work challenged or was different from competitors (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F03 Single-Market Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that aired or ran in a single country / region / market. The work should describe how the campaign was designed for the specific target market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the work was designed/adapted for the market (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F04 Social Behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work inspired by a specific audience or community, relying on identifiable social behaviour. The work should demonstrate how leveraging insights into consumer behaviour can create a powerful connection with a brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the social behaviour that inspired the work (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F05 Use of Humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that celebrates the art of humour in branded communications. Infusing wit, satire, and cleverness into campaigns that provide amusement and create memorable, laughter-inducing connections with audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the humour insight that inspired the work (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F06 Breakthrough on a Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative use of modest budgets and/or resources in relation to the market and/or industry to create maximum impact. The work should demonstrate how fresh insight, smart spending and compelling strategic thinking solved a business problem despite limited resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide budget details (overall budget, breakdown, how maximised reach vs expenditure) and explain impact; confidential information can be placed in confidential field (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F07 Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose-driven work/brand activism that addresses social, ethical and environmental issues. The work should demonstrate how the brand’s purpose has created value and affected communities by connecting customers to culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how purpose inspired the work, evidence of impact on communities, society or environment (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F08 Market Disruption
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands that have creatively adapted their strategy in response to local / regional / global issues, embracing new ways of delivering their brand while showing consideration for the consumer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how market disruption inspired the work (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category F09 Cultural Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Work that honours marketers who craft strategic solutions rooted in the lived experiences of culturally grounded communities. This approach reflects and translates the nuances of customs, behaviours, and traditions that shape foundational perspectives on identity (e.g. disability, gender, race, orientation, age).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the specific cultural insight that drove the nuanced engagement (150 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 1: Why is this work relevant for PR?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why this work is relevant for PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 100 words. This question is compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 2: Brand Context
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any brand and cultural context that would help the jury understand any cultural, national or regional nuances applicable to this work. Outline why this piece of work was created for this particular brand, in this market, at this particular moment in time, with all of the cultural and market conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 250 words. This question is compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 3: Objective(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and explain the objective(s) that were most important when creating this work. What the work set out to achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants must link results back to each selected objective. No word limit. This question is compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 4: Summary of the work
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a summary of your entry: describe the background and context, creative challenges faced, overview and analysis of effectiveness, and how objectives were met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. This question is compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 5: Describe the creative idea (20% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the creative idea and how it earns attention and transcends the original challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: cross-boundary thinking, surprise/continued attention, transcendence of original challenge, breakthrough thinking, demonstration of how the idea was designed to earn attention from the target audience. Word limit: 150 words. This question is compulsory and contributes 20% of the vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 6: Describe the PR strategy (30% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the PR strategy and execution decisions taken to achieve the objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: how effectively concept was brought to life; specific PR implementation strategies; channels utilised and their suitability; scale of execution relative to objectives; adaptation to unexpected challenges. Word limit: 150 words. This question is compulsory and contributes 30% of the vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 7: Describe the PR execution (20% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the PR execution and how the concept was implemented across channels and touchpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: how effectively the concept was brought to life; specific implementation strategies; channels and their optimality; scale relative to objectives; adaptation to changes. Word limit: 150 words. This question is compulsory and contributes 20% of the vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Question 8: List the impact and results (30% of vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: List the impact and results and link them back to the objectives selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider: performance against brand metrics (awareness, engagement), change in consumer behaviour, indications of short/medium/long-term sales success (shareholder value, profit, ROI, sales), brand health improvement and potential changes in regulations or societal/economic events. Word limit: 250 words. This question is compulsory and contributes 30% of the vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI usage disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Was Artificial Intelligence (AI) used in the work or the entry materials? If yes, you must disclose how it was used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose: what AI tools were used; extent of AI use in the final work; data sources or inputs for AI elements and where they originated. Refer to the LIONS Integrity Handbook for guidance. Misrepresentation or wilful omission may result in withdrawal. Word limit: 150 words. This question is compulsory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainability context (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline how this piece of work aligns with the brand's sustainability strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider environmental cost (steps to measure/reduce footprint), meaningful claims and evidence, long-term commitments and benchmarks used to measure contribution to the overall strategy. No word limit. Optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity, representation and accessibility (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe consideration given to representation and diversity of the team(s) involved and what consideration was given to accessibility in the work and the role of DEI thinking throughout development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No word limit. Optional; include where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information for the Jury (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are additional results you wish to disclose to the Jury but prefer to keep confidential, provide them here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Use for results you want judged but kept private.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: C01 Research, Data & Analytics (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide evidence of how the research, insight and use of data enhanced the campaign output. Consider data and/or insights gathering and interpretation, data targeting, data and/or insight integration and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for C01 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: C02 PR Effectiveness (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the effectiveness of the PR campaign: achievement of results against KPIs, effect of PR activities on brand awareness, measurable impact of the PR effort on client's objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for C02 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F01 Local Brand (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please comment on how the brand resonated with a specific target audience in a single locality or market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F01 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F02 Challenger Brand (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us about how the work challenged or was different from the brand's competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F02 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F03 Single-Market Campaign (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us how the work was designed/adapted for a single country / region / market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F03 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F04 Social Behaviour (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us about the social behaviour that inspired the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F04 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F05 Use of Humour (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us about the humour insight that inspired the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F05 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F06 Breakthrough on a Budget (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget Details: provide budget details showing how the campaign achieved breakthrough results on a limited budget. Consider overall budget, breakdown of costs, how the campaign maximised reach vs expenditure, and the significant impact this adjustment had on the campaign's effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as much context as possible; confidential information may be entered in the confidential field. Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F06 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F07 Corporate Purpose & Social Responsibility (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us how the brand purpose inspired the work. Explain how the purpose is ingrained in the core values and mission of the brand’s DNA and discuss the impact of these initiatives on communities, society or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F07 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F08 Market Disruption (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us how market disruption inspired the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F08 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific question: F09 Cultural Engagement (entry prompt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please tell us about the specific cultural insight that drove the nuanced engagement behind this work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word limit: 150 words. Compulsory for F09 entries.
